lines.c1: Scrum and Kanban both make work visible on a board.
lines.c2: Both aim for steady delivery and constant improvement.
lines.k1: Scrum works in fixed-length sprints, committing to a goal up front.
lines.k2: Kanban is a continuous flow: new work is pulled in when there is capacity.
lines.l1: Scrum limits work by time. Kanban limits it with a work-in-progress limit.
lines.l2: Scrum protects the sprint from change. Kanban welcomes change at any time.
lines.m1: Scrum prescribes roles and events. Kanban prescribes none.
lines.m2: Scrum tracks velocity. Kanban tracks cycle time.
lines.w1: Choose Scrum for product work that benefits from a steady rhythm.
lines.w2: Choose Kanban when work arrives unpredictably, like support or operations.
lines.w3: Many teams blend both, often called Scrumban.
lines.outro: Pick the rhythm that fits the work.
